absent: AUSENTE: netfs inode container layout and size reader helpers and cache cookie lifecycle and writeback queue handling.
AUSENTE: pipe data path for reads writes splice and merge accounting and ring resize and blocking behavior.
AUSENTE: poll table allocation and wait registration and wakeup and timeout and signal handling.
AUSENTE: enabled proc entry creation lookup removal and permission and hidepid enforcement details.
AUSENTE: quota hash lookup and format file IO and transaction locking and grace enforcement.
AUSENTE: watch queue loss handling and fasync delivery and user accounting for pipes.
AUSENTE: dquot reference counting and dirty writeback scheduling and statistics aggregation.

findings.text: Path container holds a mount pointer called mnt together with a dentry pointer called dentry and carries layout randomization.
Cleanup helper called __free_path_put aliases path_put for automatic release.

Default pipe depth PIPE_DEF_BUFFERS equals 16. Flags PIPE_BUF_FLAG_LRU and PIPE_BUF_FLAG_ATOMIC and PIPE_BUF_FLAG_GIFT and PIPE_BUF_FLAG_PACKET and PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE and PIPE_BUF_FLAG_WHOLE equal hex 01 and 02 and 04 and 08 and 10 and 20, meaning LRU membership and atomic mapping and gifted page and packet mode and merge allowed and whole read required.

Loss indicator PIPE_BUF_FLAG_LOSS equals hex 40 and signals message loss after the buffer. Preallocation limits PIPE_PREALLOC_MAX and PIPE_PREALLOC_KEEP equal 8 and 2 pages. Pipe size PIPE_SIZE equals PAGE_SIZE.
Pipe slot holds a page pointer called page plus an offset called offset plus a length called len plus an operations pointer called ops plus state bits called flags plus a private word called private.
Index union offers a combined head tail word called head_tail or separate indexes called head and tail. Element type called pipe_index_t is unsigned int in one build and unsigned short in another.
Anonymous pipe cache holds a fixed page pointer array called pages sized by PIPE_PREALLOC_MAX together with a racy count called count.

Pipe state holds a mutex called mutex and read wait called rd_wait and write wait called wr_wait with embedded head tail indexes and limits called max_usage and ring_size and accounting called nr_accounted and counts called readers and writers and files and r_counter and w_counter and an edge trigger flag called pseudo_edgetrigger with optional loss note called note_loss and a preallocation cache called prealloc and async pointers called fasync_readers and fasync_writers and a slot array called bufs and an owner called user with optional watch queue called watch_queue. Loss note and watch queue exist only when CONFIG_WATCH_QUEUE is enabled.

Pipe operations table offers confirm for content validation returning zero on success or negative error and release after full consumption and try_steal for page ownership transfer returning boolean with locked page for cache insertion and get for reference acquisition returning boolean.
Steal helper reports false when try_steal is missing and otherwise delegates to that hook with pipe and buffer and returns its outcome.

Stack budgets define MAX_STACK_ALLOC as 832 and FRONTEND_STACK_ALLOC as 256 with SELECT_STACK_ALLOC and POLL_STACK_ALLOC aliasing frontend and WQUEUES_STACK_ALLOC as remainder after frontend and N_INLINE_POLL_ENTRIES as remainder divided by entry size.
Default mask DEFAULT_POLLMASK combines EPOLLIN and EPOLLOUT and EPOLLRDNORM and EPOLLWRNORM. Time limit MAX_INT64_SECONDS equals maximum signed 64 value divided by HZ minus one.

Poll callback type called poll_queue_proc takes file plus wait head plus table. Table called poll_table holds a callback called _qproc with a key called _key. Entry holds a file called filp with a key called key and a wait node called wait and a wait address called wait_address.

Poll collection holds a table called pt plus a page list called table plus a task called polling_task plus a triggered flag plus an error plus an inline index called inline_index plus an inline array called inline_entries sized by N_INLINE_POLL_ENTRIES.
Requested events helper returns all bits set when the table pointer is null and otherwise returns stored _key.

Proc operations table holds flags called proc_flags with open called proc_open and read called proc_read and iterated read called proc_read_iter and write called proc_write and seek called proc_lseek and release called proc_release and poll called proc_poll and control called proc_ioctl with optional compat control called proc_compat_ioctl and map called proc_mmap and unmapped area called proc_get_unmapped_area and carries layout randomization. Flag bits mark permanent and read iter present and compat control present and seek present and forced lookup at bit zero and one and two and three and seven, with permanent zero when MODULE is defined and one otherwise, and seek required unless nonseekable_open is used.

Hide identifiers HIDEPID_OFF and HIDEPID_NO_ACCESS and HIDEPID_INVISIBLE and HIDEPID_NOT_PTRACEABLE equal 0 and 1 and 2 and 4, with the last limiting to ptraceable tasks. Pid only modes PROC_PIDONLY_OFF and PROC_PIDONLY_ON equal 0 and 1.

Proc mount info holds a namespace called pid_ns plus a group called pid_gid plus mounter credentials called mounter_cred plus a hide mode called hide_pid plus a pid only mode called pidonly plus deferred free head called rcu.

Write callback type called proc_write_t returns integer status for file plus buffer plus length. Sequence data macro called proc_create_seq_data delegates to sequence private creation with zero size. Inode private accessor called pde_data returns i_private. Network creation macro called proc_create_net delegates to network data creation with NULL data.

When proc support is disabled, root initialization and pid flushing do nothing, while symlink and directory and mount point and data directory creators return null, and sequence private and sequence data and single data and network data and network single creators expand to null, and generic create and data create return null, and size and user setters and removal helpers do nothing with subtree removal reporting zero, while parent data accessors trap and pid fd conversion reports bad file.
Disabled private data access traps instead of returning a pointer, and pid fd conversion fails with a bad file error pointer.

Quota type enum defines USRQUOTA and GRPQUOTA and PRJQUOTA as 0 and 1 and 2 for user and group and project. Masks QTYPE_MASK_USR and QTYPE_MASK_GRP and QTYPE_MASK_PRJ shift one by type. Identifier type qid_t is 32 bit and size type qsize_t is signed 64 bit. Container kqid unions uid and gid and projid with a type discriminator.

Identifier builders construct kqid from namespace plus type plus numeric value and an invalid variant from type alone and direct wrappers from uid or gid or projid, trapping on unknown type. Mapping check reports true unless conversion yields all ones.

Sizing macros DQUOT_INIT_ALLOC and DQUOT_INIT_REWRITE and DQUOT_DEL_ALLOC and DQUOT_DEL_REWRITE take maxima of versioned values. Get mask DQF_GETINFO_MASK combines root squash and system file while set mask DQF_SETINFO_MASK allows only root squash. Dirty flag DQF_INFO_DIRTY shifts one by a private base. Dquot bits DQ_MOD_B and DQ_BLKS_B and DQ_INODES_B and DQ_FAKE_B and DQ_READ_B and DQ_ACTIVE_B and DQ_RELEASING_B and DQ_LASTSET_B equal 0 through 7, with six further bits after last set reserved for quotactl set mask.

Usage block holds dqb_bhardlimit and dqb_bsoftlimit and dqb_curspace and dqb_rsvspace and dqb_ihardlimit and dqb_isoftlimit and dqb_curinodes with dqb_btime and dqb_itime. Info holds dqi_format with dqi_fmt_id and dqi_dirty_list and dqi_flags and dqi_bgrace and dqi_igrace and dqi_max_spc_limit and dqi_max_ino_limit with dqi_priv.

Dirty list uses dq_list_lock while flags and grace intervals use dq_data_lock and maxima stay static. Dquot hash and inuse and free and dirty links use dq_list_lock with disk offset stable after set under dq_lock and usage protected by dq_dqb_lock with IO serialized by dq_lock.

Dirty helper tests the info dirty bit. Statistics enum orders DQST_LOOKUPS and DQST_DROPS and DQST_READS and DQST_WRITES and DQST_CACHE_HITS and DQST_ALLOC_DQUOTS and DQST_FREE_DQUOTS and DQST_SYNCS with terminal _DQST_DQSTAT_LAST. Statistics container holds plain stat array and per cpu counter array. Increment and decrement helpers adjust the per cpu counter by type.

Dquot holds hash node called dq_hash with inuse link called dq_inuse and free link called dq_free and dirty link called dq_dirty and IO mutex called dq_lock and usage spinlock called dq_dqb_lock and reference count called dq_count and superblock called dq_sb and identifier called dq_id and disk offset called dq_off and flag word called dq_flags with embedded usage called dq_dqb.

Format table offers check_quota_file with read_file_info and write_file_info and free_file_info for file lifecycle plus read_dqblk and commit_dqblk and release_dqblk for block IO plus get_next_id for iteration. Dquot table offers write_dquot with alloc_dquot and destroy_dquot and acquire_dquot and release_dquot and mark_dirty and write_info for persistence and lifecycle plus get_reserved_space and get_projid and get_inode_usage and get_next_id for queries.

Dquot moves from allocation through read and active to modified, with warned flags for block and inode excess and fake mode for usage only and releasing queue before cleanup, while set mask bits record quotactl fields until the format clears them.

Size writer updates local size with remote size and zero point together. Resizer optionally refreshes remote size and only lowers zero point when the new size is smaller. Cookie accessor returns cache when caching is enabled and null otherwise. IO waiter blocks until the IO count reaches zero.

Context initializer stores operations and seeds remote size from current size and sets zero point to maximum and clears flags and IO count and nulls cache when enabled and prepares writeback queue and spinlock, aligning zero point to remote size and marking always release when zero point mode is requested.

Thirty two bit symmetric multiprocessing uses a sequence counter with preemption disabled, while thirty two bit preemptible builds use preemption control alone, and other builds use release stores paired with acquire loads to order page changes before size visibility.

Remote size changes only when a server change is flagged. Resize never raises zero point. Initial zero point is maximum normally and remote size when zero point mode is selected. Page release drives zero point.

Buffer contents are validated before use, with failure reported as error, and consumed buffers are released. Ownership may move to a caller with a locked page for insertion elsewhere, and references may be taken. Missing steal support is reported as failure.
Unknown quota type selection traps. Loss marking signals data loss after a buffer. Whole mode demands a full buffer return or an error. Packet mode forces packet oriented reads.
Each header defines a once guard to prevent double inclusion.

Poll state tracks the polling task with triggered and error indicators and an inline consumption index. Inline capacity follows stack budget. Default readiness covers input and output with normal data in both directions.
